clause.text: 1. Form of Sponsorship. During the term of this Agreement, Tickets shall be MP3.com's exclusive partner/source for sports, entertainment, and travel tickets, and MP3.com shall include a Tickets Portal on the "Music" page and the "Pop," "Rock" and "Alternative" genre pages on the Website. A "Portal" is defined as a web graphic with the dimensions not to exceed 125 x 125 pixels and 20Kb in size. The content of the Portal shall be supplied by Tickets and shall conform with reasonable technical and content specifications supplied by MP3.com.

reviews.rationale: The clause grants MP3.com an exclusive arrangement under which Tickets is designated MP3.com's exclusive partner/source for sports, entertainment and travel tickets during the Agreement term. The relevant policy is the no-exclusivity position, which prefers an entirely non-exclusive relationship and, at most, permits exclusivity limited to named products, a named territory and no more than twelve (12) months, lapsing on failure to meet minimum performance targets stated in the Order Form. This clause is drafted as open-ended exclusivity: it runs for the whole term without a stated cap, territory, or performance-target lapse, and no Order Form terms are provided to supply those limits. Exclusivity also restricts Tickets from serving other customers or partners, implicating the no-customer-non-solicit policy. Although the header labels this a non-compete clause, the operative obligation is exclusive dealing rather than a post-termination non-compete; no restriction on competing after the Term is stated, so the non-compete-bounded position is not the applicable policy and its risk_if_absent is not applied here. Material uncertainty: the Agreement is not supplied, so the term length, defined territory, any Order Form performance targets, and any renewal or termination provisions are unknown; also, the retrieved positions do not define whether exclusivity of this kind is measured in calendar or fixed-day periods, and no dates are given. If the term is short (e.g., an initial term of three months), whether any cap is satisfied cannot be determined from the text, because calendar months are not fixed-day periods and no dates establish actual duration. Until those dates exist, no conclusion can be drawn that the exclusivity meets or breaches a 90-day or other day/months boundary. On the supplied evidence, the exclusivity is unbounded as to duration, territory and performance conditions, so the deviation from the policy is material and the risk is high.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement is non-exclusive. Each party remains free to provide to, procure from, or contract with any third party for services of the same or a similar kind, without restriction and without any obligation to the other party.

Any exclusivity granted under this Agreement is limited to the named products, the named territory and a period of no more than twelve (12) months, and lapses if the exclusive party fails to meet the minimum performance targets stated in the Order Form.
Neither party is restricted from contracting with, soliciting or serving any customer, partner or supplier of the other party, whether during the Term or afterwards.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Any exclusivity granted under this Agreement is limited to the named products, the named territory and a period of no more than twelve (12) months, and lapses if the exclusive party fails to meet the minimum performance targets stated in the Order Form.
reviews.verification_reason: The assessment is supported. The clause expressly states that 'Tickets shall be MP3.com's exclusive partner/source' during the Agreement term, so the exclusivity claim is grounded. The cited no-exclusivity policy prefers a non-exclusive relationship and its fallback permits exclusivity only for named products, named territory, ≤12 months, with performance-target lapse; the clause contains none of these limits, supporting the deviation and high risk. The reviewer correctly treats the no-exclusivity position as applicable and explains why the non-compete-bounded position is not applied. The no-customer-non-solicit policy is reasonably referenced as implicated by exclusivity restricting Tickets from serving other customers/partners. The suggested fallback matches the cited no-exclusivity fallback verbatim. The rationale properly distinguishes the clause's open-ended exclusivity from the policy's requested limits, and does not improperly conclude that a three-month term would comply with a 90-day limit; it notes that calendar months and fixed-day periods differ and that actual dates are absent.

clause.text: 2. Impressions. MP3.com agrees to deliver a guaranteed minimum of 3,000,000 Impressions per month for the term of this Agreement. An "Impression" is defined as the display of the Tickets Portal to a user on one of the above referenced pages.

reviews.rationale: The clause creates a guaranteed minimum Impressions commitment of 3,000,000 per month. The relevant policy position [no-minimum-commitment] prefers no minimum volume commitment; its fallback contemplates that any minimum commitment be stated in an Order Form, capped at a written committed amount, with shortfall liability limited to the difference. The clause states a fixed guaranteed minimum but does not tie it to an Order Form, cap, or limited shortfall remedy, so it deviates from both the preferred and fallback positions. The exposure is residual and negotiable rather than a wholesale missing protection, since a defined committed volume is present and quantified. Separately, the clause defines 'Impression' as the display of the Tickets Portal to a user but does not define measurement, reporting, verification, or makegoods for shortfalls, which are within the same scope. Note a boundary uncertainty on duration: the clause states '3,000,000 Impressions per month for the term' but gives no dates or term length, and calendar months are not fixed-day periods; without actual dates it cannot be determined whether any month overlaps or equals a stated 90-day maximum or whether monthly limits are equivalent across months of different length. That uncertainty does not change the classification here because no term-length cap is present in the clause.

reviews.verification_reason: The assessment accurately reflects the clause: it creates a guaranteed minimum of 3,000,000 Impressions/month, defines 'Impression,' and lacks Order Form tie, cap, or limited shortfall remedy. These contract claims are supported. Policy claims match the cited [no-minimum-commitment] position: preferred no-minimum stance and fallback language requiring Order Form statement, written cap, and shortfall limited to the difference. The suggested fallback is verbatim identical to the cited fallback text. The rationale correctly distinguishes preferred versus fallback and notes deviations. The boundary-uncertainty discussion properly treats months vs fixed-day periods and does not assert that 3 months complies with a 90-day maximum; it explicitly says no such determination can be made and that no term-length cap is present. The medium risk rating is a reasoned downward adjustment from the 'high' risk-if-absent due to the presence of a quantified commitment, though somewhat lenient, it is not unsupported as a comparative judgment.

reviews.rationale: The clause sets a fixed installment schedule tied to the Effective Date in monthly increments plus a 1.5% monthly late fee. The directly relevant retrieved position is payment-net-30, which requires undisputed invoices to be payable within 30/45 days of receipt with a good-faith dispute withholding right; this clause does not establish invoice-based due dates tied to receipt or any dispute-withholding mechanism, leaving limited residual exposure. Regarding boundaries, the clause uses 'one month' through 'five months' rather than fixed-day periods; absent actual dates, whether the first installment equals or exceeds a 90-day period cannot be determined, and the duration uncertainty must be stated rather than assumed equivalent to 30/90 days. No price-increase, minimum-commitment, revenue-share, or liability-cap issue is raised by the clause text, so those positions are not applied.

The treatment of 'one month' through 'five months' is appropriate: it does not assert equivalence to 90 days and expressly notes that actual dates would be needed to determine compliance. The medium risk level follows from a relevant-but-not-fully-matched position. The suggested fallback matches the playbook fallback verbatim. No unsupported contract or policy claim is present.

clause.text: 4. Term and Termination. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall remain in full force and effect until one (1) year subsequent to the Effective Date, provided however, that Tickets may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon thirty (30) days' notice to MP3. com at any time prior to the expiration of sixty (60) days subsequent to the Effective Date. Furthermore, for a thirty (30) day period, beginning thirty (30) days prior to the first anniversary of this Agreement, Tickets shall have the right to renew the Agreement for another year with Sponsor Fees that do not exceed a [***] percent increase over the existing Sponsor Fees. Any payments which have accrued prior to the date of termination shall remain due and payable. Sections 6, 7, and 8 shall survive termination of this agreement.

Furthermore, for a thirty (30) day period, beginning thirty (30) days prior to the first anniversary of this Agreement, Tickets shall have the right to renew the Agreement for another year with Sponsor Fees that do not exceed a [***] percent increase over the existing Sponsor Fees. Any payments which have accrued prior to the date of termination shall remain due and payable. Sections 6, 7, and 8 shall survive termination of this agreement.

reviews.rationale: The clause grants Tickets a unilateral termination for convenience (30 days' notice, exercisable only until 60 days after the Effective Date), whereas the termination-for-convenience preferred position contemplates a mutual right and the fallback a mutual 60-day notice period. This one-sided deviation is a limited, negotiable exposure (medium), not a prohibition breach. The renewal provision (a 30-day window beginning 30 days before the first anniversary for Tickets to renew at a capped fee increase) aligns directionally with the renewal-opt-in fallback, which allows renewal for successive 12-month terms unless written non-renewal notice is given at least 30 days before term end; the clause's mechanism is a preferential opt-in renewal window rather than a non-renewal notice, so the wording differs from the fallback but does not by itself create high risk. The survival of Sections 6, 7, and 8 and the preservation of accrued payments are bounded post-termination obligations consistent with the post-termination-wind-down position. The clause uses calendar months ('thirty (30) days', 'sixty (60) days', 'one (1) year') without fixed dates or day-count definitions; because calendar-month periods are not fixed-day periods, the exact policy boundary (e.g., whether the notice or renewal timing satisfies a day-based standard) cannot be confirmed from the text alone, and the compliance of the notice periods with any day-specific benchmark is uncertain. That boundary uncertainty, combined with the unilateral convenience right, supports medium risk. No cited position sets a 90-day maximum, so no 90-day benchmark is asserted.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party, without penalty or further liability other than for amounts accrued prior to the effective date of termination.
reviews.verification_reason: The assessment is largely supported but contains unsupported/incorrect claims. (1) The renewal analysis is misapplied: the clause gives only Tickets a unilateral right to renew within a specific 30-day window at a capped increase, whereas the cited renewal-opt-in fallback describes automatic successive 12-month renewal subject to either party's non-renewal notice and a 5% fee cap. The clause neither states that renewal is automatic nor that it requires both parties' written agreement; characterizing the clause as merely a different 'mechanism' and aligned 'directionally' overstates the alignment and understates the deviation. (2) The post-termination claim is unsupported: the clause only preserves accrued payments and survival of Sections 6, 7, and 8. It does not provide transition assistance, data return/deletion, or a bounded 60/90-day wind-down as in the cited position. Stating the survival and accrued-payment terms are 'consistent with' the post-termination-wind-down position is inaccurate; at most they partially address survival, but the position's core transition/data obligations are absent. (3) The suggested fallback is verbatim correct, but the rationale should distinguish clause mechanics from playbook requests more precisely. Also, the rationale's discussion of calendar months/fixed days is not tied to any cited day-based maximum and the final sentence correctly notes no 90-day benchmark exists, so that part is not itself a violation; it is merely unnecessary. Correct the renewal and post-termination comparisons and reassess risk accordingly.

5. Measurement. Upon request, Tickets shall have access to pertinent statistics related to Impressions covering the period of this contract. Tickets agrees to accept MP3.com's measurement of Impressions (the "Count") according to MP3.com's logs and other tracking devices and/or software MP3.com may use, provided however, that Tickets shall have the right to audit MP3.com's records in this regard. reviews.rationale: The clause grants Tickets audit rights over MP3.com's records limited only by a material-interference standard, with no frequency cap or prior-notice requirement. The closest relevant playbook position, audit-rights-bounded, prefers at most one audit per twelve months on thirty days' notice at the auditing party's cost, and fallback permits at most two audits per twelve months on fifteen days' notice. The clause's cost-shifting trigger (auditor determines overstatement by more than five percent) is consistent with the fallback's five-percent cost-shift concept, but the absence of any frequency or notice bound is a limited, negotiable deviation rather than a critical gap. The confidentiality and payment-net-30 positions are not applicable to these audit mechanics. Material uncertainty: whether the clause sits within a contract requiring audits relevant to this Agreement, and the extent to which the omitted frequency/notice limits can be added by negotiation, are not established by the supplied text.

reviews.rationale: The clause is an indemnification provision. It is mutual and limited to each party's own site content/conduct, which aligns with the mutual-indemnity preferred position. However, subsection (c) extends indemnity to "any other act, omission or representation by either party" — far broader than the playbook's "to the extent arising from its own breach of this Agreement or its negligence" — and the clause contains no liability cap or reference to the Agreement's limitations of liability, whereas the playbook's preferred and fallback mutual indemnity are expressly subject to the limitation of liability. The indemnity is therefore potentially uncapped and, combined with the broad (c) trigger, creates material exposure. The clause also lacks the express linkage to the liability cap required by liability-cap-fees and liability-uncapped-carve-outs (which treat indemnification as an uncapped carve-out). Note: the duration/period question is not present here; no month/day equivalence issue arises from this clause.

citations.excerpt: Each party shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the other party against third-party claims to the extent arising from its own breach of this Agreement or its negligence, subject to the limitations of liability set out in this Agreement.

Each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

The limitations of liability in this Agreement shall not apply to a party's indemnification obligations, breach of confidentiality, or liability arising from its fraud, gross negligence or willful misconduct. No other exclusion from the cap applies.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Each party shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the other party against third-party claims to the extent arising from its own gross negligence or willful misconduct, subject to the limitations of liability set out in this Agreement.
reviews.verification_reason: The assessment is supported. The clause is indeed a mutual indemnification provision limited in scope to each party's site content/conduct for subsections (a) and (b), and subsection (c)'s 'any other act, omission or representation by either party' is correctly identified as far broader than the playbook's 'own breach of this Agreement or its negligence' standard. The clause contains no liability cap or reference to limitations of liability, so the observation that it is potentially uncapped is accurate, and the playbook preferred/fallback both condition indemnity on the limitations of liability. The citations of mutual-indemnity, liability-cap-fees, and liability-uncapped-carve-outs are used consistently with their stated positions and 'high' risk-if-absent levels, supporting the 'high' risk conclusion. The rationale properly distinguishes what the clause states from what policy requests, and the suggested fallback matches the mutual-indemnity fallback text verbatim. The note that no month/day equivalence issue arises is also correct, since no period/duration term appears in the clause.

reviews.rationale: Clause 7 mutually excludes special, indirect, incidental, and consequential damages, and its section 6 exception for representations, warranties, and indemnity claims is an explicit term (section 6 exists in the supplied excerpt). Against the liability-no-consequential-damages preferred position, however, the exclusion omits punitive damages and loss of profits, revenue, goodwill, or data. Because the clause does not address those categories, they are not excluded or limited by this clause; whether they are capped or uncapped is not established by the supplied text, so this is a missing protection rather than an affirmative unlimited-liability term. The section 6 carve-out cannot be assessed against liability-uncapped-carve-outs because section 6 is a representations/warranties and indemnity provision, and the provided excerpt is truncated before the full indemnity terms are shown. The deviation from the preferred mutual exclusion is a negotiable gap rather than a full absence of the protection.
